claims.statement: `collectSessions(roots, now)` in `app/src/main/scanners/index.ts` is the module's single public entry point: it takes a caller-supplied `{tool name: data root}` mapping plus an injected wall-clock time in seconds (production passes `defaultSessionRoots()`, tests pass temporary fixture roots and a fixed `now`), and it returns the merged list of `SessionInfo` records sorted by age ascending.

Per-tool dispatch is one lookup in the module-level `SCANNERS: Record<string, Scanner>` (`qoder`/`hermes`/`zcode`/`kimicode`/`kimiwork`); a root whose key is absent is skipped with no log line at all, registering a new tool means adding an entry there plus its default root in `defaultSessionRoots()`, and the record stays mutable enough that the seam test registers a deliberately throwing scanner in it.

Every scanner invocation is wrapped in its own `try`/`catch`: a failing scanner emits one `console.warn` line naming the tool and the error (`agent-sessions: <tool> 扫描失败，跳过：…`) and contributes no sessions, while the other tools in the same call still scan.

`makeSession(tool, sid, project, age, state, options)` in `app/src/main/scanners/types.ts` fixes the normalized record shape to exactly `tool`/`id`/`project`/`running`/`age`/`tasks_done`/`tasks_total`/`state` (the shared `SessionInfo` contract): it rounds `age` to seconds, defaults `running` to `age <= RUNNING_WINDOW` unless the scanner overrides it, and maps absent task data to `null` — distinct from a real `0/0` count, with `tasks_done` itself able to be `null` beside a positive total when zcode's `SUM` group is all NULL.
Session identity is `tool` + `id`, chosen as the front-end DOM diff key because ids from different tools can collide and would otherwise overwrite each other's row.

Two constants in `app/src/main/scanners/types.ts`, re-exported from `scanners/index.ts`, are the single definition behind every window decision: `RUNNING_WINDOW = 90.0` (age at or below it counts as running) and `ACTIVE_WINDOW = 600.0` (anything strictly older leaves the list, while the boundary itself is still listed). Window and state decisions run on the unrounded age, and the seam tests derive their boundary instants from the fixture file's mtime plus these constants.

The shared four-state vocabulary is RUN/CONFIRM/DONE/IDLE, but only the qoder scanner derives all four via `sessionState(age, role, kind)`: RUN wins inside the running window, otherwise an assistant tail ending in `tool_use` yields CONFIRM, an assistant text tail yields DONE and anything else yields IDLE, so non-qoder rows can never show CONFIRM — the accepted distortion recorded in ADR-0003.

Evaluation of the qoder state split relies on `sessionLast`, which reads at most the last 128 KB of the session jsonl through `readTail`, walks the lines downwards and classifies the newest `assistant`/`user` record (kind `user` for a user record, `tool` when the assistant content list ends in a `tool_use` block, otherwise `text`); lines that fail to parse are skipped, and a file with no recognizable record or an unreadable file yields no role/kind, which degrades to IDLE outside the running window while the session is still listed from its mtime.

The qoder scanner's row source `qoderJsonlRows` enumerates `projects/*/*.jsonl` with the file stem as the session id, uses the jsonl mtime for age and drops anything past `ACTIVE_WINDOW`, and `scanQoder` then enriches each row with task counts from `tasks/<session id>/` and a project name.

Archived sessions are excluded inside the scanners before the seam sees them: hermes skips rows whose `archived` column is truthy and zcode skips rows with a non-null `time_archived`, so reaped or archived work never reappears inside the active window.

hermes is the strongest signal source: RUN is true when the session id appears in the active-lease file `runtime/active_sessions.json` (which keeps an old unended session running across write gaps) or when `end_reason` is null and activity is within 90 s; an ended session is DONE even when recent, and an unended quiet session is IDLE. Age comes from `last_activity_at` falling back to `started_at`, and rows where both are null are dropped.

hermes tolerates a corrupt lease file: `hermesLeases` catches any read or parse failure of `runtime/active_sessions.json` and returns an empty lease set — silently, with no log line — so the tool still returns its sessions, just without lease-based RUN promotion.

zcode judges liveness from the explicit millisecond timestamp `time_updated`, converted as `now - time_updated / 1000`, with no further heuristic than the shared window, and derives per-session progress from the `todo` table with one grouped query (`SUM(status = 'completed')` and `COUNT(*)` by `session_id`), defaulting to `(0, 0)` for a session with no todos and to a null done count when the `SUM` group is all NULL.
zcode subagent sessions are filtered out inside the scanner by the `sess_subagent_` id prefix (`ZCODE_SUBAGENT_PREFIX`) because they dominated real data as list noise, so they never reach the seam.

kimi code derives age from the newer of `state.json` and `agents/main/wire.jsonl` mtimes (so an actively written wire log keeps a session RUN even when the state file is stale), emits only RUN/DONE, and degrades per session: a `state.json` that cannot be read or parsed skips that session while the tool's other sessions are still returned.

kimi work is a deliberately degraded scanner: it joins `conversation-statuses.json` with `conversation-context-usage.json`, requires both a status entry and a non-empty `updatedAt` for a conversation to appear, takes age from that per-conversation timestamp rather than any file mtime, maps `status === 'completed'` to DONE and unknown values to IDLE, uses the last colon-separated segment of the map key as the id, and leaves `project` empty with null tasks because the conversation bodies and titles live in upstream private storage.

Degradation granularity differs by scanner and by failure kind: kimi work parses both JSON maps before any filtering, so a broken file raises out of the scanner and skips the whole tool, whereas kimi code skips only the affected session for an unreadable or unparseable `state.json`; a thrown type violation — a kimi code `state.json` that parses into a non-object, hermes activity or zcode `time_updated` that are not numbers, kimi work's invalid ISO `updatedAt` — escapes the row loop and skips the whole tool.

SQLite-backed scanners open their databases through the shared `openReadOnly` helper, which uses `new DatabaseSync(dbPath, { readOnly: true })` — the `node:sqlite` equivalent of the Python `file:…?mode=ro` URI named by ADR-0003 — plus `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 500` (closing the handle and throwing if that pragma fails); the short busy timeout makes a database held exclusively by its own writer fail fast into the silent-skip path instead of stalling the 1 Hz sampling round, and missing or corrupt database files therefore skip just that tool.

Project display names come from two helpers with different fallbacks: `projectName` scans the last 64 KB of a qoder jsonl for a `cwd` (taking its win32 last path segment) and falls back to the jsonl's parent directory name, while `dirName` takes the win32 last segment of a stored path and returns an empty string when the value is not a non-empty string (e.g. a kimi code session without `workDir`); hermes and zcode route their stored directory through `dirName` as well.

The ADR records that the tools' liveness signals are not equally trustworthy and accepts a tiered accuracy: hermes is most accurate (lease file plus explicit end reason), zcode is next (explicit timestamps plus an archived flag), and kimi code is coarsest (pure file mtime); the agreed remedy for a tool that flickers because of sparse writes is to widen that tool's own window rather than change the unified model.

The test strategy treats `collectSessions` as the only automated seam: each scanner has its own vitest module under `app/tests/scanners/` that builds disposable fixture roots (temporary directories, minimal SQLite schemas and status/usage JSON through the shared `fixtures.ts` builders) plus a fixed `now`, asserting only external behavior such as state mapping, window boundaries, exclusions, ordering and task counts, and never touching real user directories or scanner internals.

`SessionsService` is the seam's only caller: it resolves its data roots once at construction (`options.roots ?? defaultSessionRoots()`) and exposes `refresh(now)` for one sampling round plus `current()` for the last result; when an entire round fails unexpectedly it logs `deck-sessions: 本轮扫描意外失败，给空表：…` and stores an empty list instead of keeping the previous one, so no stale rows survive a failed round.

`defaultSessionRoots(home = os.homedir())` is the single place the five production data roots are spelled out (`~/.qoder-cn`, `~/AppData/Local/hermes`, `~/.zcode`, `~/.kimi-code`, `~/AppData/Roaming/kimi-desktop/kimi-agent`); they are not configurable through `config.json`, and callers override them only through the kernel `sessionRoots` option or the service `roots` option.

The collection round runs once per second outside the module: the in-process kernel timer calls `bridge.tick()`, which refreshes the panel data port (`sessions.refresh()` plus `desktop.refresh()`) and pushes `panel/changed`, while the production data-plane kernel calls `sessions.refresh()` on its own 1 Hz timer inside the utility process and posts the resulting snapshot to the panel process for the renderer.

The sessions card consumes the records directly: `tool` becomes a two-letter tag (QD/KC/KW/ZC/HM, unknown tools `??`) and is also the routing key sent to `session/focus` on click, `state` becomes a lowercase CSS class, `project` becomes the row name, and `tasks_done`/`tasks_total` render as `NNN/NNN` only when both are non-null; the header shows the full session count while at most nine rows are drawn, and an empty list shows the standby text.

No scanner has a write path into a tool's store, and the SQLite scanners select metadata only — hermes never selects `title`/`ended_at` and zcode never selects `title` or the todo `content` — while JSON stores are read with `readFileSync` or an `openSync`/`readSync` tail read.

The Qoder status block was retired in ticket 03: the `qoderStatus` helper, the `QoderStatus` type, the `qoder` panel-snapshot section and the `qoder` plugin capability were removed, while the Qoder session row (QD tag, inline `tasks_done`/`tasks_total` progress, click-through) and the shared `taskStats`/`projectName`/`sessionLast`/`sessionState`/`qoderJsonlRows` helpers were kept — which leaves `taskStats(...).current` computed but without any consumer.

`taskStats(sessionId, root)` is qoder-specific: it counts the parseable `tasks/<session id>/*.json` files as total, counts `status === 'completed'` as done, and returns the first `in_progress` subject as `current`; it is reachable only from `scanQoder` and the module re-export, and `scanQoder` uses just the `done`/`total` pair for the session row's inline progress.
